cues.en: You know, I'm really puzzled by something.
cues.zh: 你知道，有件事真让我挺困惑的。
现在已经是 2026 年了，

cues.en: believe it or not, and even though we live in this modern digital world where we can ask our smart assistants to close the blinds for us, we're still excited about finding oil.
cues.zh: 不管你信不信，哪怕身处动动嘴就能让智能助手帮我们关窗帘的现代数字世界，我们依然会因为发现石油而兴奋不已。

cues.en: That feels weird to me. Petroleum is a nineteenth century technology and here in the twenty first century,
cues.zh: 这让我觉得很不可思议。石油是 19 世纪的技术，而现在已经是 21 世纪了，

cues.en: very few of the things we use are powered by petroleum products.
cues.zh: 我们日常使用的东西里，已经很少靠石油产品来驱动了。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: why are we still so obsessed with finding more oil?
cues.zh: 为什么我们还这么执着于寻找更多石油？

cues.en: Well, there's a very simple reason.
cues.zh: 其实原因很简单。

cues.en: It just has to do with how oil as a technology works.
cues.zh: 这纯粹跟石油这项技术本身的运作方式有关。

cues.en: Once we find new crude oil deposits and take some out of the ground, we then refine that oil into many useful products and things.
cues.zh: 一旦发现新的原油储量并开采出来，我们就会把它提炼成各种各样有用的产品。

cues.en: However, by far, the greatest portion of it is used to produce gasoline and diesel fuel, which power some of the machines we rely on.
cues.zh: 但其中绝大部分，都被用来生产汽油和柴油，为我们赖以生存的机器提供动力。

cues.en: Now those machines are great and have unlocked plenty of wonderful new possibilities for us, even whole new kinds of economies.
cues.zh: 这些机器确实很棒，为我们开启了无数美妙的新可能，甚至催生了全新的经济形态。

cues.en: While they've also come with some downsides that concern me and I think deserve more weight in our public conversations,
cues.zh: 尽管它们也带来了一些令人担忧的弊端，我认为这些弊端应该在公众讨论中获得更多关注，

cues.en: you're not gonna hear me tell you to stop using your machines. That is not at all what this video is about.
cues.zh: 但我也绝不会劝大家别用机器。这个视频根本不是要讲这个。

cues.en: But petroleum
cues.zh: 但是石油

cues.en: has an unavoidable issue which is easy to ignore but I don't think you should.
cues.zh: 存在一个无法回避的问题，人们很容易忽视它，但我觉得不该忽视。

cues.en: It's disposable
cues.zh: 它是一种一次性的

cues.en: energy.
cues.zh: 能源。

cues.en: In order for our machines to do things for us like take us to work or get the kids to school,
cues.zh: 为了让机器替我们干活，比如载我们上班，或者接送孩子上学，

cues.en: they burn the fuels which power them.
cues.zh: 它们必须燃烧为自己提供动力的燃料。

cues.en: That makes those fuels single use,
cues.zh: 这就让这些燃料变成了一次性消耗品，

cues.en: one and done.
cues.zh: 用完即尽。

cues.en: So to keep using those machines, which most of us would like to do,
cues.zh: 所以为了继续使用这些机器——大家也确实想继续用——

cues.en: we have no choice but to keep finding more oil to make more fuel.
cues.zh: 我们别无选择，只能不断寻找更多石油来制造更多燃料。

cues.en: Many of us have come to the conclusion that this is a serious problem for a long list of reasons.
cues.zh: 出于种种原因，许多人都得出结论：这已经成了一个严重的问题。

cues.en: For one thing, it makes our standard of living dependent on an extremely intensive resource extraction process which, since what that process yields will be burned shortly after it's created,
cues.zh: 一方面，它让我们的生活水平依赖于极其高强度的资源开采，而由于开采出来的产物造出来不久就会被烧掉，

cues.en: appears to have no end in sight.
cues.zh: 这种开采似乎永远望不到尽头。

cues.en: Additionally,
cues.zh: 此外，

cues.en: because oil deposits inevitably run dry, we often rely on extraction efforts happening in other countries,
cues.zh: 由于油田终究会枯竭，我们常常要依赖其他国家的开采，

cues.en: which may or may not be friendly.
cues.zh: 而那些国家未必对我们友好。

cues.en: And while oil is relatively easy to store,
cues.zh: 虽然石油相对容易储存，

cues.en: meaning we can build reserves of oil,
cues.zh: 意味着我们可以建立石油储备，

cues.en: we use it a lot faster than you may realize.
cues.zh: 但我们消耗它的速度可能远超你的想象。
我们 7.14 亿

cues.en: barrel strategic oil reserve sounds huge,
cues.zh: 桶的战略石油储备听起来很庞大，

cues.en: but it only holds enough to sustain slightly more than a month of our current use.
cues.zh: 但按目前的消耗速度，它也仅够支撑一个多月。

cues.en: That's not a very long time.
cues.zh: 这可撑不了多久。

cues.en: And even when we know we have a healthy and secure supply of oil,
cues.zh: 而且，即便我们确信石油供应充足且安全，

cues.en: that oil costs a lot of money to find, extract, and refine into the fuels we buy to power our machines.
cues.zh: 勘探、开采并将其提炼成供机器驱动的燃料，也要耗费极其昂贵的资金。

cues.en: That results in those fuels being fairly expensive to purchase as a consumer, and that results in a high and ongoing
cues.zh: 这导致消费者购买这些燃料时相当昂贵，也导致任何使用它们的机器面临高企且持续的

cues.en: operating cost for any machines which use them. And that cost can change quite dramatically based on supply and demand.
cues.zh: 运行成本。而且这项成本会随供需剧烈波动。

cues.en: What's worse, since nearly every step in our economy currently involves something going on a truck which burns diesel fuel,
cues.zh: 更糟的是，目前我们经济中几乎每个环节，都涉及某些东西要靠烧柴油的卡车运输，

cues.en: spikes in oil prices make their way into virtually everything we buy.
cues.zh: 油价飙升会传导到我们购买的几乎每一样东西上。

cues.en: For those struggling to make ends meet, that can be the difference between well fed and not, even if they don't drive a car.
cues.zh: 对勉强维持生计的人来说，这可能是吃饱与吃不饱的区别，即使他们不开车。

cues.en: I truly believe that an honest assessment of the basic realities of using petroleum as a source of energy
cues.zh: 我真心相信，对把石油作为能源的基本现实做一次诚实评估，

cues.en: suggests that our situation is actually quite precarious.
cues.zh: 会表明我们的处境其实相当岌岌可危。

cues.en: And if nothing else, it can really hurt the wallet sometimes.
cues.zh: 至少，有时候它真的很伤钱包。

cues.en: But on that note, there's good news.
cues.zh: 不过说到这儿，也有好消息。

cues.en: We've developed an enormous variety of electric machines which don't use fuels to function at all.
cues.zh: 我们已经开发出种类繁多的电动设备，它们完全不靠燃料运行。

cues.en: For instance, the screen you're looking at right now and in fact nearly everything in your home.
cues.zh: 比如你现在正看着的屏幕，事实上还有你家里的几乎所有东西。

cues.en: While today we still burn fuels to generate electricity,
cues.zh: 尽管今天我们仍在燃烧燃料发电，

cues.en: the even better news is that we don't have to do that anymore.
cues.zh: 更好的消息是，我们再也不必这样做了。

cues.en: We know how to build devices which generate electricity from nothing but sunlight.
cues.zh: 我们知道如何制造只靠阳光发电的设备。

cues.en: And though it has escaped the notice of many politicians,
cues.zh: 虽然许多政客没有注意到这一点，

cues.en: we also know how to build cost effective rechargeable and recyclable batteries
cues.zh: 我们也知道如何制造高性价比、可充电、可回收的电池，

cues.en: which can be charged from the sun to store that energy for use whenever you'd like,
cues.zh: 它们能靠阳光充电，把能量存起来，供你随时使用，

cues.en: even at night when the sun isn't shining.
cues.zh: 甚至在没有阳光的夜晚也行。

cues.en: The bad news?
cues.zh: 坏消息呢？

cues.en: There are a whole lot of people spending money and time trying to confuse everyone and convince us that everything I just said is a pie in the sky idea which can never ever work.
cues.zh: 有很多人花钱花时间，试图把所有人搞糊涂，让我们相信我刚说的一切都是永远不可能实现的空中楼阁。

cues.en: But I have never believed those people.
cues.zh: 但我从来不信那些人。

cues.en: Why?
cues.zh: 为什么？

cues.en: Simple.
cues.zh: 很简单。

cues.en: I'm a Midwesterner.
cues.zh: 我是中西部人。

cues.en: Most of us that were born and raised here grew up learning the virtue of long term thinking,
cues.zh: 我们大多数在这里出生、长大的人，从小就学到长期思维的美德，

cues.en: something that seems to be less and less popular these days.
cues.zh: 而这东西如今似乎越来越不吃香了。

cues.en: My upbringing taught me to value things like durability and resilience and to consider those factors when making important life decisions.
cues.zh: 我的成长经历教会我重视耐用性和韧性，并在做重大人生决定时考虑这些因素。

cues.en: Midwesterners are also big believers in getting the most value out of what we spend our money and time on.
cues.zh: 中西部人也非常相信，要把花出去的钱和时间用出最大价值。

cues.en: And we have learned that in many cases,
cues.zh: 而且我们明白，在很多情况下，

cues.en: the best value comes from spending more money upfront on things which let you spend less money later.
cues.zh: 最大的价值来自前期多花钱，买那些能让你以后少花钱的东西。

cues.en: That old fashioned midwestern wisdom of frugality
cues.zh: 那种老派的中西部节俭智慧，

cues.en: is what makes me so confident that we should be installing much more renewable energy capacity and quickly.
cues.zh: 正是它让我如此确信，我们应该建设多得多的可再生能源装机容量，而且要快。

cues.en: I didn't need scientific studies or lectures on climate change to form that opinion.
cues.zh: 我形成这个看法，并不需要气候变化方面的科学研究或讲座。

cues.en: I just know a good deal when I see one.
cues.zh: 我只是看到好买卖就认得出来。

cues.en: The energy we capture from renewable sources like solar and wind power
cues.zh: 我们从太阳能和风能等可再生能源中捕获的能量，

cues.en: doesn't cost anything.
cues.zh: 是完全免费的。

cues.en: And while the batteries we will use to support those sources are expensive to purchase,
cues.zh: 虽然用来配套这些能源的电池采购成本很高，

cues.en: batteries can be used many, many more times than a gallon of gasoline can.
cues.zh: 但电池可重复使用的次数，远非一加仑汽油所能比拟。

cues.en: Today's battery chemistries are pushing 5,000
cues.zh: 如今的电池化学体系在彻底损耗前，

cues.en: charge cycles before they wear out, meaning they'll last well over a decade before they need to be recycled.
cues.zh: 已经能达到近 5000 次充放电循环，这意味着它们能用上十几年才需要回收。

cues.en: And the future of batteries looks even brighter than that with different chemistries extending lifespans,
cues.zh: 而且电池的前景还要更广阔：新的化学成分正在不断延长寿命、

cues.en: lowering costs, and reducing the use of harmful or hard to find materials in the construction of battery cells.
cues.zh: 降低成本，并在电芯制造中减少有害或稀缺材料的使用。

cues.en: These factors combined tell a clear story to me, which says renewable energy paired with long lasting and reusable energy storage
cues.zh: 这些因素结合在一起，向我传递了一个明确的信息：可再生能源搭配长寿命、可重复使用的储能系统，

cues.en: is the best deal out there, and we'd be foolish to pass it up.
cues.zh: 是目前最划算的方案，放着不用就太傻了。

cues.en: I would even go so far as to say that at this point, anyone who says otherwise is either lying to you to protect their own interests
cues.zh: 我甚至可以说，到了今天，任何持相反观点的人，要么是在为了维护自身利益对你撒谎，

cues.en: or simply hasn't been paying attention to what things look like today.
cues.zh: 要么就是根本没有关注如今的现状。

cues.en: the levelized cost of solar and storage, which includes the costs of purchasing both the panels and the batteries,
cues.zh: 光储平准化度电成本（包括采购光伏板和电池的全部成本），

cues.en: is now lower than any other kind of energy production we know of.
cues.zh: 已经低于我们已知的任何其他能源生产方式。

cues.en: That seemed like the inevitable outcome to me for years because the sun is free,
cues.zh: 多年来这在我看来都是必然的结果，因为太阳光是免费的，

cues.en: but for a long time, panels were very expensive.
cues.zh: 但很长一段时间里，光伏板都非常昂贵。

cues.en: Today, solar panels and batteries are now cheap enough to make that outcome real now.
cues.zh: 而如今，光伏板和电池已经足够便宜，让这一愿景成为了现实。

cues.en: And solar power is just one source of renewable energy.
cues.zh: 况且太阳能还只是可再生能源的一种。

cues.en: I believe that a renewable energy future should excite you because it allows us to harvest energy,
cues.zh: 我相信可再生能源的未来足以让你兴奋，因为它让我们能够“收获”能量，

cues.en: not extract it.
cues.zh: 而不是“开采”能量。

cues.en: And once you really interrogate that difference,
cues.zh: 一旦你真正理解了这二者的本质区别，

cues.en: the noise goes away and the puzzle solves itself.
cues.zh: 所有的杂音都会消散，谜题自然迎刃而解。

cues.en: Before I really get started, and yes, this video is quite long, isn't it? I have to make a few things clear.
cues.zh: 在正式开始前——没错，这个视频确实挺长的，对吧？——我得先澄清几件事。

cues.en: First, this video has two very distinct audiences in mind, and which one of those two I'm speaking to may not be entirely clear at any given moment.
cues.zh: 首先，这个视频预设了两个截然不同的受众群体，在某一时刻我究竟在对谁说，可能并不总是显而易见。

cues.en: I'm telling you this because if you think you know where I'm going with something,
cues.zh: 之所以提前说明，是因为如果你以为猜到了我的结论，

cues.en: you might be surprised.
cues.zh: 结果可能会出乎你的意料。

cues.en: For example,
cues.zh: 比如，

cues.en: this video is not trying to sell you anything like solar panels or home energy storage.
cues.zh: 这个视频绝对不是想向你推销光伏板或家用储能设备。

cues.en: Whenever I'm talking about renewable energy,
cues.zh: 每当我聊起可再生能源，

cues.en: people seem to think that's where I'm leading, but as a matter of fact, I do not have solar panels on my roof,
cues.zh: 大家总觉得我是在带货，但事实上，我自家屋顶上根本没装光伏板，

cues.en: and for various reasons, I personally don't even want to add them.
cues.zh: 而且出于各种原因，我个人甚至完全不想装。

cues.en: I don't think any of us should have to put more thought into how we use electricity than we do right now, But I do think we should be moving as much of our energy demand to the electric grid as we can and we should be doing that more and faster.
cues.zh: 我觉得大家在用电这件事上，完全没必要操比现在更多的心；但我确实认为，我们应该尽可能把更多的能源需求转移到电网上，而且动作应该更大、更快。

cues.en: I hope by the end you'll understand why I feel that way. And again, it might not be what you think.
cues.zh: 我希望到最后大家能明白我为什么这么想。而且说实话，原因可能跟你想的不太一样。

cues.en: Second, there are going to be lots of comments down below which say things like, but what about the batteries? And a lot of them will be coming from a place of good faith.
cues.zh: 第二，评论区肯定会有很多人问：“那电池怎么办？”其中很多确实是出于善意的疑问。

cues.en: But lots of people ask that question in bad faith. And I would like you to know that anyone leaving those sorts of comments here
cues.zh: 但也有很多人是恶意抬杠。我想让大家知道的是，在这儿发这类评论的人，

cues.en: probably didn't watch this video.
cues.zh: 大概率根本没看这个视频。

cues.en: What about the batteries is one of the central questions I intend to address.
cues.zh: “电池怎么办”正是我打算重点讲的核心问题之一。

cues.en: There's a lot of people being told to worry about things which I, for one, don't think you should be worrying much about. And I promise that I'll explain why I feel that way when we get there.
cues.zh: 很多人被灌输去担心一些事情，但依我看，这些其实完全没必要瞎操心。我保证讲到那里时，会解释为什么我有这种看法。

cues.en: And thirdly,
cues.zh: 第三点，

cues.en: I'm going to be talking a lot about cars since many people have a deep connection to them and they are the biggest reason we use so much oil.
cues.zh: 我会花不少篇幅聊聊汽车，因为汽车与大家的生活息息相关，而且也是我们消耗巨量石油的最主要原因。

cues.en: And,
cues.zh: 而且，

cues.en: well, since electric cars now exist in large numbers, we can easily compare what a battery powered world looks like to a petroleum powered one, both in functionality and cost.
cues.zh: 既然现在电动汽车已经相当普及，我们就能很方便地在功能和成本上，把电池驱动的世界和燃油驱动的世界做个对比。

cues.en: Cars are just kind of the perfect tool to understand this at this moment, at least in my view.
cues.zh: 至少在我看来，汽车是眼下理解这个问题的绝佳切入点。

cues.en: But the logic of this video can and I think should be applied to literally anything which burns any kind of fossil fuel.
cues.zh: 但这个视频的逻辑，完全可以、而且我认为也应该套用到任何消耗化石燃料的事物上。

cues.en: For instance, I still heat my home with natural gas, and natural gas has the exact same problems as oil.
cues.zh: 比如，我家供暖依然用天然气，而天然气面临着和石油完全一样的问题。

cues.en: Since my furnace sets it on fire, it's a disposable,
cues.zh: 既然我家的锅炉是直接把它烧掉，那它就是一种一次性的、

cues.en: costly, single use fuel we have to keep digging out of the ground if I want to keep using the furnace.
cues.zh: 昂贵的一次性燃料，我要想继续取暖，就得源源不断地从地下把它挖出来。

cues.en: It just happens to be delivered to my home through a metered pipe rather than sold at fueling stations in a pay as you go scheme.
cues.zh: 它只不过是通过装了表的管道送到我家，而不是在加油站随加随付罢了。

cues.en: But with those things out of the way, let's get back to oil.
cues.zh: 交代完这些背景，我们再回到石油上来。

cues.en: We use crude oil for lots of things, but the most significant thing we use it for in The US is for producing refined gasoline
cues.zh: 原油的用途五花八门，但在美国，它最主要的用途还是提炼汽油，

cues.en: for motor cars.
cues.zh: 供汽车使用。

cues.en: So let's talk about the pinnacle of motor cars. This 2010 Nissan Cube. Hey, isn't that the car you bought to make videos on engine management technology?
cues.zh: 那我们来聊聊汽车界的巅峰之作——这辆 2010 款的 Nissan Cube。诶，这不是你买来做发动机管理技术视频的那辆车吗？

cues.en: Yes.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: When is that happening?
cues.zh: 那期视频啥时候出啊？

cues.en: We're getting there.
cues.zh: 快了快了。

cues.en: Oh, carry on then.
cues.zh: 行吧，你继续。

cues.en: Now, if you were paying close attention to the intro, this section might feel a bit repetitive, and I apologize if it does, but there are two core facts about using this car which I'd really like you to think deeply about and confront.
cues.zh: 如果你刚才认真看了开场，可能会觉得这部分有点重复，真是这样的话我先道个歉；但关于开这辆车，有两个核心事实，我真心希望大家能好好琢磨并正视一下。

cues.en: The first fact is that as this car does its job of providing transportation,
cues.zh: 第一个事实是，在它履行代步工具的职责时，

cues.en: it burns the gasoline that's inside its fuel tank.
cues.zh: 它会烧掉油箱里的汽油。

cues.en: This means you constantly have to replace that fuel if you want to keep driving the car.
cues.zh: 这就意味着，要想一直开下去，你就得不停地给它补充燃料。

cues.en: That's easy enough to do, but the second core fact about using this car is that it costs you money every time you replace that fuel.
cues.zh: 这做起来不难，但使用这辆车的第二个核心事实是：每次补充燃料都要花钱。

cues.en: I know you already know both of those facts,

cues.zh: 现在你可能会好奇，为什么我之前会说自己不想在自家屋顶装太阳能板。

cues.en: Well, the quickest way to answer that is to go on a field trip. Behind me is a 27 megawatt solar farm that was built here in the town of Depew, Illinois.
cues.zh: 要回答这个问题，最直接的办法就是实地看看。我身后是伊利诺伊州 Depew 镇建起的一座 27 兆瓦太阳能电站。

cues.en: Now there's a couple notable things about that. First, Illinois is not exactly the solar power capital of the country. It's cloudy as I'm filming this and we're kinda high up in the latitudes.
cues.zh: 这里有几点值得注意。首先，伊利诺伊州绝非全美的太阳能之都。我拍摄时天正阴着，而且这里的纬度也偏高。

cues.en: And yet,
cues.zh: 但即便如此，

cues.en: there's a 27 megawatt solar farm that got built into Pew, Illinois.
cues.zh: 依然有一座 27 兆瓦的太阳能电站落户在了伊利诺伊州的 Depew。

cues.en: Why did that happen?
cues.zh: 为什么会这样？

cues.en: Well, because people who like to make money understand the difference between CapEx and OpEx.
cues.zh: 因为想赚钱的人都明白 CapEx（资本支出）和 OpEx（运营支出）的区别。

cues.en: And so do you, even if you don't know what those terms mean.
cues.zh: 其实你也明白，即便你还不知道这两个术语是什么意思。

cues.en: I'll explain them shortly, but first, do you know anyone with a backup generator?
cues.zh: 我稍后会详细解释，但在此之前，你认识有谁家里备了发电机吗？

cues.en: That question might sound out of left field, but I promise you it's a perfect way to understand this.
cues.zh: 这个问题听起来可能有点突兀，但我保证，这是理解它的绝佳角度。

cues.en: Some people live where the electricity grid isn't as reliable as they'd like it to be.
cues.zh: 有些人住的地方，电网并没有想象中那么可靠。

cues.en: Everyone hates power outages because electricity is extremely important to our lives at this point. And if grid reliability is poor enough where someone lives, they might elect to install a large backup generator powered by natural gas which will automatically kick on and generate electricity during a power outage.
cues.zh: 没人喜欢停电，毕竟现在电对我们的生活太重要了。如果某地电网实在不稳定，有些人就会选择安装大型天然气备用发电机，在停电时自动启动发电。

cues.en: When someone decides to spend their money that way, that's CapEx or capital expenditure.
cues.zh: 决定把钱花在这上面，就属于 CapEx，即资本支出。

cues.en: They are using their capital to buy a durable thing which will last them many years, and it becomes an investment in the future.
cues.zh: 他们用资本购买了一件能用很多年的耐用品，这也成了一项面向未来的投资。

cues.en: Some folks install generators which are large enough to power their entire home,
cues.zh: 有些人装的发电机功率很大，足够带动全家的用电，

cues.en: meaning power outages are nothing but an inconvenient blip.
cues.zh: 这意味着停电对他们来说不过是一阵小插曲。

cues.en: And that leads to what I think is an interesting and revealing question to ponder.
cues.zh: 这就引出了一个我认为非常有趣且发人深省的问题。

cues.en: If those people own a machine which can power everything in their home by itself,
cues.zh: 如果他们拥有一台单靠自己就能带动全家所有电器的机器，

cues.en: why don't they get their money's worth out of it and just use that machine all the time? Why stay connected to the power grid at all?
cues.zh: 为什么不把它用回本，一直开着它呢？为什么还要连着电网？

cues.en: Well, that's because that machine needs fuel to generate electricity
cues.zh: 这是因为发电机发电是需要燃料的，

cues.en: and that fuel costs money which makes it part of OpEx which is short for operating expenditure.
cues.zh: 而燃料是要花钱的，这就属于 OpEx，也就是运营支出。

cues.en: The gas company will charge you for the gas that generator uses and those fuel costs mean that using a backup generator is much more expensive than pulling energy directly from the power grid.
cues.zh: 燃气公司会按发电机的用气量收费，这些燃料成本意味着，用备用发电机比直接从电网用电要昂贵得多。

cues.en: Everyone with a backup generator knows this,
cues.zh: 有备用发电机的人都清楚这一点，

cues.en: and that's why it's a backup and not their primary source of electricity.
cues.zh: 这也是为什么它只是“备用”，而不是主力供电来源。

cues.en: It is simply too expensive to use that machine all the time.
cues.zh: 一直用它实在太烧钱了。

cues.en: The great big machines on the power grid,
cues.zh: 电网里那些庞大的发电机组，

cues.en: even when they're burning the same natural gas as a backup generator,
cues.zh: 即便烧的是跟备用发电机一样的天然气，

cues.en: can capture much more of the energy contained in the fuel they burn and turn it into electricity
cues.zh: 也能从燃料中转化出远多于后者的电能，

cues.en: than the small engine inside a Generac can.
cues.zh: 绝非 Generac 这种发电机里的小引擎能比的。

cues.en: That efficiency of scale is what makes generating electricity cheaper for grid scale power stations.
cues.zh: 正是这种规模效应带来的高效率，让电网级电站的发电成本低得多。

cues.en: And the fact that the wires which connect your house to the grid are already there and were paid for perhaps decades ago
cues.zh: 加上连接你家和电网的输电线路早已铺好，成本可能几十年前就结清了，

cues.en: explains why distributing that energy through the power grid is very efficient both economically and from an energy perspective.
cues.zh: 这就解释了为什么通过电网输送电力，无论从经济还是能效角度来看都极其高效。

cues.en: And what's really important to remember is that grid power is cheaper despite the fact that the people who operate natural gas plants are making a healthy profit.
cues.zh: 更重要的是要记住：即便天然气电厂的运营方赚取了丰厚的利润，电网供电依然更便宜。

cues.en: They're not just running a power plant for the fun of it, they're in business.
cues.zh: 他们建电厂可不是为了做慈善，而是在做生意。

cues.en: But the smarter business critters out there know that even with the benefits of scale,
cues.zh: 但更精明的商业老手知道，即便具备规模优势，

cues.en: a natural gas plant still has a very high opex.
cues.zh: 天然气电厂的运营成本依然极高。

cues.en: Each unit of electricity a gas plant generates requires burning expensive fuel which eats into profits.
cues.zh: 燃气电厂每发一度电，都要燃烧昂贵的燃料，这会侵蚀利润。

cues.en: So for those who have an eye on making money,
cues.zh: 所以对那些一心想赚钱的人来说，

cues.en: when solar farms pop up and demonstrate that we can produce electricity with no input costs at all,
cues.zh: 当光伏电站纷纷涌现，并证明发电完全可以零原料成本时，

cues.en: well, gas doesn't look so great anymore.
cues.zh: 燃气发电看起来就没那么诱人了。

cues.en: See, all a solar farm operator needs to do is sell their electricity for slightly less than it costs a competing natural gas plant to make it, and that's what they'll do.
cues.zh: 你看，光伏电站运营商只需把电价定得比竞对燃气电厂的发电成本稍低一点就行，他们也确实是这么做的。

cues.en: That's good for consumers because that makes electricity cheaper to use,
cues.zh: 这对消费者来说是好事，因为用电成本更低了，

cues.en: but because the solar farm has next to zero opex,
cues.zh: 但由于光伏电站的运营成本几乎为零，

cues.en: it still generates a healthy profit even though it's cheaper.
cues.zh: 即便价格更便宜，它依然能带来可观的利润。

cues.en: And savvy business people who think long term will use those profits to build more solar farms.
cues.zh: 而那些有长远眼光的精明商人，会用这些利润去建更多的光伏电站。

cues.en: The basic realities of economics mean that photovoltaics
cues.zh: 基础的经济规律意味着，光伏技术

cues.en: are, at this point,
cues.zh: 在当下，

cues.en: frankly unstoppable.
cues.zh: 坦白说已经势不可挡了。

cues.en: The sun doesn't cost any money to use which means all of the energy a solar panel produces is free.
cues.zh: 利用太阳能不需要花一分钱，这意味着太阳能板发出的每一度电都是免费的。

cues.en: And that means whatever price you can sell that energy for on the power grid energy market is almost purely profit once the panels have been paid off.
cues.zh: 这也意味着，一旦面板收回了投资成本，在电网能源市场上卖出的每一分钱几乎都是纯利润。

cues.en: Best of all, grid scale energy storage in the form of electrochemical
cues.zh: 最棒的是，电化学电池形式的

cues.en: batteries has gotten cheap enough that it is now possible today to build a solar farm with batteries that can produce energy twenty four seven
cues.zh: 电网级储能已经足够便宜，如今建造带储能的光伏电站完全可以做到全天候 24 小时供电，

cues.en: and all the while doing that for a lower cost than any other source of electricity.
cues.zh: 而且全过程的成本比任何其他电力来源都要低。

cues.en: And since both photovoltaic panels and batteries are manufactured
cues.zh: 加上光伏面板和电池都是在

cues.en: in factories which can leverage economies of scale,
cues.zh: 可以发挥规模经济优势的工厂里生产的，

cues.en: they're just gonna keep getting cheaper to manufacture.
cues.zh: 它们的制造成本只会越来越低。

cues.en: The economics are already in favor of solar and storage,
cues.zh: 经济账本就已经倾向于光伏加储能了，

cues.en: but they're gonna keep looking better and better every year.
cues.zh: 而且未来只会一年比一年更划算。

cues.en: Solar energy has put us on the cusp of a positive feedback loop,
cues.zh: 太阳能已经让我们站在了正反馈循环的风口上，

cues.en: yet relatively few people seem to have realized this.
cues.zh: 但似乎很少有人意识到这一点。

cues.en: And that's despite the fact that... There's another one not even five miles up the road here in Spring Valley, Illinois.
cues.zh: 尽管事实摆在眼前……就在伊利诺伊州斯普林瓦利前面不到五英里处，就又有一座。

cues.en: Solar farms are starting to pop up everywhere,
cues.zh: 光伏电站开始在各地涌现，

cues.en: even in states like Illinois,
cues.zh: 甚至在伊利诺伊这样的州也是如此，

cues.en: because the business case simply makes so much sense.
cues.zh: 因为这种商业模式实在是太划算了。

cues.en: It's farming a crop just like we do with land today,
cues.zh: 这就像我们在土地上耕种农作物一样，

cues.en: but that crop gets harvested every single day rather than once a year, and virtually no work is involved in harvesting that crop.
cues.zh: 只不过这种“作物”每天都在收获，而不是一年一次，而且收割几乎不需要费任何力气。

cues.en: Plus, the crop doesn't need inputs in the form of water or fertilizer or pesticide or seed.
cues.zh: 此外，这种“作物”也不需要水、化肥、农药或种子等任何投入。

cues.en: You just plop some panels on some land, angle them to get the most energy out of the sun as you can, and let the money roll in.
cues.zh: 你只需把面板往地上一架，调好角度尽可能多地获取太阳能，然后就可以坐等收钱了。

cues.en: This is a capitalist's wet dream.
cues.zh: 这简直是资本家的终极梦想。

cues.en: People are always talking about passive income as if that's a panacea.
cues.zh: 人们总在谈论被动收入，仿佛它是万灵药。

cues.en: Well, there it is.
cues.zh: 喏，这就是了。

cues.en: You can become a farmer and all you'll have to do is mow the grass between the panels a few times a year. The fact that there's this amazing business opportunity out there is why solar farms are happening in the first place.
cues.zh: 你可以去当个“农夫”，一年里只需要在光伏板之间割几次草。正是因为有这么好的商机，太阳能电站才得以兴起。

cues.en: And they're leveraging the power grid we already have which can move energy from one place to another.
cues.zh: 而且它们利用的是现有的电网，能够将电能从一处输送到另一处。

cues.en: And that's why I'm not that interested in putting panels on my roof.
cues.zh: 这也是为什么我不太想在自己家屋顶上装太阳能板。

cues.en: Yes. There are good arguments for distributing energy resources
cues.zh: 没错，发展分布式能源确实有很多充分的理由，

cues.en: and we have a real problem right now with getting new transmission lines permitted.
cues.zh: 而且我们目前在新建输电线路审批上面临着现实难题。

cues.en: There are a ton of solar power projects which are already funded
cues.zh: 有大量的太阳能项目资金都已经到位了，

cues.en: but aren't happening because FERC can't get their act together and they're stuck in permitting hell.
cues.zh: 却迟迟无法落地，因为 FERC 办事不力，项目全都卡在漫长痛苦的审批里。

cues.en: NIMBYs aren't helping either.
cues.zh: NIMBY 们（邻避分子）也没帮上什么忙。

cues.en: Pushing individuals to install solar on their rooftop is one way to bypass some of these issues and it does have some advantages,
cues.zh: 推动个人在屋顶安装太阳能板确实能绕开部分问题，也确实有一些优势，

cues.en: but many people don't have the agency to install solar on their roof even if they wanted to and could afford it.
cues.zh: 但很多人即使想装且装得起，自己也没有决定权。

cues.en: Renters can't do that even if they're renting a house.
cues.zh: 租客就做不到，哪怕租的是独栋房子。

cues.en: And what's worse, apartment buildings don't have enough roof space to be self sufficient. Cities will always be relying on solar farms.
cues.zh: 更糟糕的是，公寓楼根本没有足够的屋顶空间来实现自给自足。城市将始终依赖太阳能电站。

cues.en: There are many more reasons I'm not a big fan of pushing people towards buying their own panels and batteries, which I'll spare you for time.
cues.zh: 我不赞成鼓励大家自己买光伏板和电池的原因还有很多，限于时间就不细说了。

cues.en: Bottom line, I will gladly pay these small businesses which are daring to build the future through my power bills and think that's a far more efficient use of my money.
cues.zh: 总之，我很乐意通过电费来支持那些敢于创造未来的小企业，我觉得把钱花在这要高效得多。

cues.en: But speaking of efficient uses of things, let's address some of the concerns I know many of you out there have about solar energy.
cues.zh: 不过说到资源的利用效率，我们来聊聊我知道大家对太阳能普遍存在的一些顾虑。

cues.en: Like land use.
cues.zh: 比如土地利用问题。

cues.en: Solar farms do indeed require a lot of space.
cues.zh: 太阳能电站确实需要占用大量空间。

cues.en: That 27 megawatt solar farm in Depew is on something like a 120 acre site.
cues.zh: Depew 那座 27 兆瓦的太阳能电站占地大概有 120 英亩。

cues.en: I used an online tool and drew a circle around the access road to come up with that figure, so I can't guarantee it's accurate, but that's what I'm gonna roll with.
cues.zh: 我是用在线工具顺着进出道路圈了一圈才得出这个数字的，不敢保证百分之百准确，但先姑且按这个算吧。

cues.en: Now, 27 megawatts is a tremendous amount of power,
cues.zh: 27 兆瓦确实是很大的功率，

cues.en: but in the context of the power grid, it's pretty piddly.
cues.zh: 但放到整个电网里来看，其实微不足道。

cues.en: This is the three phase line that connects the solar farm to the substation in Depew and it's,
cues.zh: 这条就是连接太阳能电站和 Depew 变电站的三相线路，它……

cues.en: well, it ain't exactly a big transmission line now, is it?
cues.zh: 呃，看起来可真算不上什么大型输电线，对吧？

cues.en: So, yeah, solar energy will use lots of land.
cues.zh: 所以，没错，太阳能确实会占用大量土地。

cues.en: However,
cues.zh: 但是，

cues.en: since I'm from Illinois,
cues.zh: 既然我来自伊利诺伊州，

cues.en: I think I'm qualified to explain why you probably don't need to worry too much about land use.
cues.zh: 我想我还是有资格来解释一下，为什么大家其实不用太担心土地占用问题。

cues.en: That is a cornfield.
cues.zh: 那是一片玉米地。

cues.en: It doesn't look like much right now because it's the middle of January, but corn used to be growing there and it was harvested in the fall.
cues.zh: 现在正值一月中旬，看着光秃秃的没什么，但这里以前种过玉米，秋天就已经收割了。

cues.en: Now, there's three very notable things about this reality.
cues.zh: 现在，这个现实中有三件非常值得注意的事。

cues.en: First of all, this land should not look like this.
cues.zh: 首先，这片土地不该是现在这个样子。

cues.en: This is Illinois. We're the prairie state. The natural environment is prairie, and now there's virtually none of that left because it has all been turned into farms.
cues.zh: 这里是伊利诺伊州。我们是草原之州。自然环境本是草原，如今几乎一点不剩，全被改成了农场。

cues.en: Secondly,
cues.zh: 其次，

cues.en: we only get one harvest per year out of this land.
cues.zh: 这片土地每年只能收获一次。

cues.en: We spend all the summer growing the corn, and then in the fall it's harvested just once.
cues.zh: 整个夏天我们都在种玉米，到了秋天只收割一次。

cues.en: If this was a solar farm, it could have a harvest every single day.
cues.zh: 如果这是太阳能农场，它每天都能有一次收获。

cues.en: And third, if you're thinking, well, what if we stop growing corn there? We can't eat anymore.
cues.zh: 第三，你可能会想：那如果我们不在那种玉米呢？我们就没得吃了。

cues.en: Well, this corn is not the corn that you eat. Some of it does end up in lots of different food products, but a large portion of this corn gets used for that.
cues.zh: 其实，这种玉米不是给人吃的玉米。有些确实进入了各种食品，但很大一部分玉米被用在了那上面。

cues.en: Yeah. Those messages on gas pumps which say may contain up to 10% ethanol?
cues.zh: 没错。加油站油泵上那些写着“可能含有最多10%乙醇”的提示？

cues.en: That came from corn.
cues.zh: 那来自玉米。

cues.en: We have been using an astonishing amount of our rich agricultural land to grow corn to feed to cars.
cues.zh: 我们一直用惊人面积的肥沃农田种玉米，只为喂给汽车。

cues.en: Maybe you remember the days of flex fuel vehicles and e eighty five being relevant.
cues.zh: 也许你还记得灵活燃料汽车和E85还有市场的日子。

cues.en: Well, back in 2005,
president George w Bush signed the Energy Policy Act of 2005.
cues.zh: George W. Bush 总统签署了《2005年能源政策法案》。

cues.en: And in 2007,
he signed the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007.
cues.zh: 他又签署了《2007年能源独立与安全法案》。

cues.en: Those acts mandated a specific amount of ethanol in gallons which needs to be produced so it can be mixed with gasoline.
cues.zh: 这些法案规定，必须生产特定加仑数的乙醇，以便与汽油混合。

cues.en: The idea, as you might have gleaned from the independence and security part, was to start making our own energy for cars so that we'd be less dependent on foreign oil.
cues.zh: 这个想法，你从“独立与安全”部分大概能猜到，就是开始为汽车自产能源，减少对外国石油的依赖。

cues.en: A policy I wholeheartedly support.
cues.zh: 这项政策我完全支持。

cues.en: The only trouble is that doing it with corn ethanol is tremendously stupid.
cues.zh: 唯一的麻烦是，用玉米乙醇来做这件事极其愚蠢。

cues.en: First of all, it's important to acknowledge that we only get one corn harvest per year.
cues.zh: 首先，必须承认我们每年只收一季玉米。

cues.en: Now, an acre of cornfield might be able to produce 550
cues.zh: 一英亩玉米地也许能产出550

cues.en: gallons of corn ethanol when all is said and done.
cues.zh: 加仑玉米乙醇，最终算下来。

cues.en: I'd like to note that it takes an awful lot of chemistry and energy to turn corn into ethanol,
cues.zh: 我想指出，把玉米变成乙醇需要大量化学处理和能源，

cues.en: but we'll just ignore that and pretend it's easy and free.
cues.zh: 但我们先忽略这点，假装它又简单又免费。

cues.en: So let's go back to that solar farm.
cues.zh: 那回到那个太阳能农场。

cues.en: If this were a 120 acre cornfield,
cues.zh: 如果这是一片120英亩的玉米地，

cues.zh: 它几乎全部的原材料质量都能轻松回收，用来做成另一块电池板。

cues.en: Which is important.
cues.zh: 这很重要。

cues.en: When it comes to the actual silicon cells,
cues.zh: 至于实际的硅电池，

cues.en: well,
cues.zh: 这个嘛，

cues.en: you've probably heard or heard someone say that these things are full of toxic materials.
cues.zh: 你可能听过，或者听人说过，这些东西充满有毒材料。

cues.en: That's misinformation
cues.zh: 那是错误信息

cues.en: and let me explain why.
cues.zh: 我来解释为什么。

cues.en: There are some kinds of solar cell that we've been experimenting with like thin film solar cells or perovskite cells which require some less than great elements in their construction.
cues.zh: 我们一直在试验某些太阳能电池，比如薄膜太阳能电池或钙钛矿电池，它们制造时需要一些不太理想的元素。

cues.en: But those represent only about 5%
cues.zh: 但那些只占大约5%

cues.en: of panels made today.
cues.zh: 的当今制造的电池板。

cues.en: The vast majority are using monocrystalline
cues.zh: 绝大多数用的是单晶

cues.en: silicon at this point, which is a material we derive from quartz.
cues.zh: 硅，目前这是我们从石英中提取的材料。

cues.en: You know,
cues.zh: 你知道，

cues.en: rocks.
cues.zh: 就是石头。

cues.en: There are some trace elements of phosphorus,
cues.zh: 这里面有一些痕量元素，磷、

cues.en: boron, and silver in here,
cues.zh: 硼和银，

cues.en: But based on what I've researched,
cues.zh: 但根据我的研究，

cues.en: the only potentially
cues.zh: 唯一可能

cues.en: harmful substance people might worry about in this is lead in the solder which makes electrical connections.
cues.zh: 让人担心的有害物质，是焊料里的铅，它负责电气连接。

cues.en: You can see some of it right here.
cues.zh: 你可以在这里看到一些。

cues.en: But I'm not actually sure that lead is even in this panel.
cues.zh: 但我其实不确定这块面板里到底有没有铅。

cues.en: We've had lead free solder for quite some time.
cues.zh: 无铅焊锡我们已经用了相当长一段时间了。

cues.en: Though, as any electronics enthusiast will tell you, it can be annoying to work with because it doesn't flow as well as when there's a little lead in the mix.
cues.zh: 不过，任何电子爱好者都会告诉你，它用起来可能很烦，因为它的流动性不如掺了一点铅的时候。

cues.en: I say that because it's possible these will always have to use lead solder to get a good bond with the silicon cells.
cues.zh: 我这么说是因为，这些面板可能永远都得用含铅焊锡，才能和硅电池片形成良好的结合。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: even if that's true,
cues.zh: 即使那是真的，

cues.en: we know how to deal with lead.
cues.zh: 我们也知道怎么处理铅。

cues.en: Did you know that new lead acid batteries are almost entirely made from old lead acid batteries?
cues.zh: 你知道吗，新的铅酸电池几乎完全是用旧铅酸电池做的？

cues.en: Every time you buy a car battery from a store, you're gonna have to pay what's called a core charge,
cues.zh: 每次你在商店买汽车电池，都得付所谓的旧件押金，

cues.en: which you don't get refunded until you bring your old battery back to the store, and that's to encourage recycling.
cues.zh: 直到你把旧电池带回店里，这笔钱才会退还，这么做是为了鼓励回收。

cues.en: This system works so well that we capture about 99%
cues.zh: 这套系统运行得非常好，我们能回收约99%

cues.en: of the material in dead car batteries.
cues.zh: 的报废汽车电池中的材料。

cues.en: We have a nearly closed loop recycling stream already established for them.
cues.zh: 我们已经为它们建立了近乎闭环的回收流程。

cues.en: That's some foreshadowing for the what about the batteries section, but I'm really saying it here to let you know we can absolutely figure out how to capture the lead in these safely and reuse it.
cues.zh: 这算是对“电池怎么办”那一节的一点伏笔，但我在这里说，其实是想告诉你们，我们绝对能想办法安全地回收这些面板里的铅并再利用。

cues.en: We just have to want to.
cues.zh: 我们只需要愿意去做。

cues.en: And speaking of recycling,
cues.zh: 说到回收，

cues.en: there's absolutely no reason we couldn't also recycle the silicon inside of these.
cues.zh: 我们也完全没有理由不回收这些面板里的硅。

cues.en: The worn out solar cells could be melted down and purified into new silicon to make new wafers to make new cells at the end of a panel's life.
cues.zh: 在面板寿命结束时，报废的太阳能电池片可以熔化并提纯成新的硅，用来制造新的硅片，再制造新的电池片。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: even if for some reason we never figure that out or it's never economically viable,
cues.zh: 即使因为某种原因我们一直没能想出办法，或者它永远不具经济可行性，

cues.en: you have to remember two things.
cues.zh: 你得记住两件事。

cues.en: First, each panel will last a quarter of a century or longer.
cues.zh: 第一，每块面板都能用25年甚至更久。

cues.en: And second,
cues.zh: 第二，

cues.en: those cells are extremely thin, usually less than 200 micrometers,
cues.zh: 那些电池片极薄，通常不到200微米，

cues.en: and thus have almost no material in them at all.
cues.zh: 因此里面几乎没有什么材料。

cues.en: I wanted to remove the cells from this panel so I could actually weigh them and tell you just how much of this panel's mass the silicon cells constitute.
cues.zh: 我想把电池片从这块面板上拆下来，好实际称一称，告诉你们硅电池片占这块面板质量的多少。

cues.en: But they're so thin and fragile that I could not peel away the coating which seals them to the glass without destroying them. I tried several different solvents hoping to dissolve some of the adhesives in here, but I had no luck at all.
cues.zh: 但它们又薄又脆，我没法在不弄坏它们的情况下剥掉把它们封在玻璃上的涂层。我试了几种不同的溶剂，希望能溶解里面的一些粘合剂，但完全没成功。

cues.en: The magic of buying two of them has unfortunately failed us.
cues.zh: 买两个的魔法不幸失效了。

cues.en: However, I has Internet.
cues.zh: 不过，我有互联网。

cues.en: Assuming a thickness of 200 micrometers,
cues.zh: 假设厚度为200微米，

cues.en: which appears to be on the thick side these days,
cues.zh: 这在这些年似乎算偏厚的，

cues.en: then if we stacked up all 72 of these cells, they'd make a stack which is just 1.4
cues.zh: 那么如果我们把这72片电池片全部叠起来，它们会形成一摞只有1.4

cues.en: centimeters tall.
cues.zh: 厘米高。

cues.en: The total volume would thus be about 94.5
cues.zh: 因此总体积大约会是94.5

cues.en: cubic centimeters.
cues.zh: 立方厘米。

cues.en: And the density of silicon is about 2.3
cues.zh: 而硅的密度约为2.3

cues.en: grams per cubic centimeter,
cues.zh: 克每立方厘米，

cues.en: meaning this solar panel has maybe 215
cues.zh: 也就是说，这块太阳能板里大约有215

cues.en: grams of silicon in it.
cues.zh: 克硅。

cues.en: That's about 3% of its total mass.
cues.zh: 这大概占其总质量的 3%。

cues.en: Now, this is only a 100 watt panel and most panels sold today are larger with more cells.
cues.zh: 这块只是 100 瓦的电池板，而如今市面上卖的大多尺寸更大、电池片更多。

cues.en: But that still means we're looking at about a kilogram of silicon per 500 watt solar panel on the high end.
cues.zh: 但这依然意味着，往高了算，一块 500 瓦的太阳能板大约含有一公斤硅。

cues.en: Now, that's not a lot for an individual panel, but if we followed through with the Korn Belt thought experiment, we'd need about 10,000,000,000 panels. So,
cues.zh: 对单块板子来说确实不算多，但如果按照“玉米带”那个思想实验推算，我们需要大约 100 亿块板子。所以，

cues.en: well, those panels are going to need something like five or 10,000,000
cues.zh: 嗯，这些电池板大概需要 500 万到 1000 万……

cues.en: metric tons of silicon.
cues.zh: 公吨的硅。

cues.en: And that is certainly a lot.
cues.zh: 这确实是个庞大的数字。

cues.en: But it's probably not as much as you might think.
cues.zh: 但可能并没有你想的那么多。

cues.en: For one thing, right now, in The US, we put some 265,000,000
cues.zh: 首先，目前在全美，我们运去填埋的……

cues.en: metric tons of stuff in landfills
cues.zh: 垃圾大概有 2.65 亿公吨，

cues.en: every year.
cues.zh: 每年如此。

cues.en: So if we simply landfilled all that silicon,
cues.zh: 所以哪怕我们把那些硅全部拿去填埋，

cues.en: which I will remind you represents the silicon necessary to completely power the entire US electricity grid from solar energy and nothing else,
cues.zh: 顺便提醒一下，这代表着完全依靠纯太阳能为整个美国电网供电所需的全部硅料，

cues.en: we'd only be taking up less than a tenth of our yearly landfill capacity by mass and we'd only need to do that every quarter of a century.
cues.zh: 按质量算，它占用的填埋量也不到我们年垃圾填埋能力的十分之一，而且每四分之一世纪（25年）才需要处理一次。

cues.en: Remember how I said I'd only need 12 of those solar panels to provide enough energy to drive my car in the winter?
cues.zh: 还记得我说过，冬天开电动车只需要 12 块这样的太阳能板供电吗？

cues.en: That's what's really important to remember.
cues.zh: 这才是最关键的一点。

cues.en: The amount of silicon or in fact whatever material in a solar panel might concern you that each person in this country will end up utilizing in this imagined future scenario
cues.zh: 在这个设想的未来场景中，全国人均消耗的硅——或者太阳能板里任何让你担心的材料——

cues.en: is very small.
cues.zh: 其实都微乎其微。

cues.en: And when you remember that each of the solar panels is gonna last a solid quarter of a human lifetime,
cues.zh: 别忘了，每块太阳能板的使用寿命实打实有人类寿命的四分之一，

cues.en: if not longer,
cues.zh: 甚至更长，

cues.en: then the amount of material used per day is irrelevant.
cues.zh: 那么平摊到每天的材料消耗量根本不值一提。

cues.en: Anyone trying to get you to focus on that is fear mongering and deflecting your attention away from the fact that currently
cues.zh: 任何试图让你盯着这点不放的人，都是在制造恐慌，试图转移你的注意力，掩盖一个事实：

cues.en: we burn through millions of barrels of oil every day.
cues.zh: 我们现在每天都在烧掉数以百万桶的石油。

cues.en: And now, here we are.
cues.zh: 那么，现在我们回到正题。

cues.en: What about the batteries?
cues.zh: 电池的问题该怎么解决？

cues.en: If we actually live in this imagined future of nothing but solar energy,
cues.zh: 如果我们真生活在这样一个纯靠太阳能的设想未来中——

cues.en: which in case it's not clear, I don't think we will because we have many different sources of energy available to us as well, but if we actually live in this future,
cues.zh: 说明一下，我觉得并不会这样，因为我们还有很多其他能源形式可用，但假设我们真生活在这样的未来——

cues.en: we have to deal with when the sun's not shining.
cues.zh: 我们就必须解决没有阳光时该怎么办。

cues.en: And we do that with batteries.
cues.zh: 而答案就是电池。

cues.en: We would be building much more solar power capacity than we can actually use when the sun is shining
cues.zh: 我们建设的太阳能装机容量，会远超日照充足时的实际用电需求，

cues.en: and the excess we're not using will charge enormous banks of batteries so that when the sun sets and the panels stop producing any output,
cues.zh: 多余的电量会用来给海量电池组充电，这样每当日落西山、光伏板不再发电时，

cues.en: we have stored energy to get us through to sunrise.
cues.zh: 我们就有储备能源撑到太阳再次升起。

cues.en: We're also gonna have long term storage available to get us through periods of bad weather.
cues.zh: 我们还会配备长时储能系统，用来度过恶劣天气。

cues.en: But of course we can also use this high-tech idea called wires and move energy from sunny deserts to cloudy places.
cues.zh: 当然，我们还可以利用一种叫作“电线”的“高科技”，把阳光充沛的沙漠地区的电力输送到阴天的地方。

cues.en: There's a huge variety of ways we could solve this issue and that's one of the cool things about electricity.
cues.zh: 解决这个问题的方法多种多样，这也是电力的奇妙之处之一。

cues.en: But no matter what, we're gonna need to build a whole heck of a lot of batteries
cues.zh: 但无论如何，我们都需要制造极其大量的电池，

cues.en: and those suckers absolutely
cues.zh: 而且这些家伙

cues.en: do have some nasty chemicals in there and we're gonna need to extract a whole lot of raw material from mines and whatnot to get them.
cues.zh: 里面确实含有一些有害化学物质，我们还得从矿山等地开采大量原材料来制造它们。

cues.en: However,
cues.zh: 然而，

cues.en: if you understand the logic of lifespan,
cues.zh: 如果你理解了使用寿命背后的逻辑，

cues.en: you'll know what I'm about to say.
cues.zh: 就会明白我接下来要说什么。

cues.en: Most people who say, but what about the batteries? Seem to always ignore two core facts about batteries.
cues.zh: 大多数质问“那电池怎么办？”的人，似乎总是忽略了关于电池的两个核心事实。

cues.en: The first fact is that they last many years now.
cues.zh: 第一个事实是，现在的电池能用很多年。

cues.en: In fact, some of the latest batteries with a daily charge cycle should get to fifteen years old before they start degrading significantly.
cues.zh: 事实上，一些最新款的电池即使每天充放电一次，也要用到 15 年后才会开始出现明显衰减。

cues.en: That's fifteen years of daily use of the same battery pack as opposed to fossil fuels which can all be used, I remind you,
cues.zh: 提醒大家一下，同一个电池组可以每天使用、持续用上 15 年，而化石燃料都只能使用——

cues.en: once.
cues.zh: 一次。

cues.en: And the second core fact is that when those batteries have degraded,
cues.zh: 第二个核心事实是，即使这些电池衰减了，

cues.en: they're still there.
cues.zh: 它们也依然存在。

cues.en: When battery cells degrade,
cues.zh: 当电芯发生衰减时，

cues.en: it's not as if the material inside of them is disappearing.
cues.zh: 并不意味着它内部的物质凭空消失了。

cues.en: What's actually happening is that the physical arrangement of those materials is slowly changing.
cues.zh: 实际发生的情况是，这些物质的物理排列结构在缓慢发生变化。

cues.en: As the reversible chemical reaction which we call charging and discharging the battery occurs inside,
cues.zh: 随着电池内部发生我们称之为“充放电”的可逆化学反应，

cues.en: little bits of material in the anodes and cathodes can start breaking off and moving around creating structures inside that eventually start to block the chemical reaction from happening and reduce the battery cell's ability to function.
cues.zh: 正极和负极上的微小材料碎屑会开始脱落、游走，并在内部形成一些结构，最终阻碍化学反应的进行，降低电芯的工作性能。

cues.en: But that does not mean any of the materials have transformed
cues.zh: 但这并不意味着里面的任何物质

cues.en: into something else.
cues.zh: 变成了别的东西。

cues.en: You can't take a lithium atom, for example, and turn it into iron.
cues.zh: 比如，你不可能把一个锂原子变成铁原子。

cues.en: All the lithium that was in there when the battery was made
cues.zh: 电池制造时放进去的所有锂，

cues.en: is still there.
cues.zh: 依然还在那里。

cues.en: So when the battery wears out,
cues.zh: 所以当电池寿命耗尽时，

cues.en: all of the lithium inside can be recovered.
cues.zh: 里面的所有锂都可以回收。

cues.en: Let's talk about mining for a second.
cues.zh: 我们再来聊聊采矿。

cues.en: When we find new deposits of some substance we're looking for,
cues.zh: 当我们发现某种所需物质的新矿藏时，

cues.en: it's not as if someone just happens upon a giant lump of pure cobalt and we start cutting chunks out of it. No. We find a deposit of ore which is rich in that material.
cues.zh: 并不是说有人碰巧发现了一大块纯钴，然后大家就开始往下切。并不是。我们找到的是富含这种物质的矿石矿床。

cues.en: Then we'll dig up that ore and do lots of fancy processing to extract the cobalt or whatever from the rest of the rocks and purify it.
cues.zh: 然后我们会把矿石挖出来，经过大量复杂的加工处理，把钴等物质从杂石中提取出来并进行提纯。

cues.en: Why am I telling you this?
cues.zh: 我为什么要说这个？

cues.en: Because the richest ore for whatever material you need to build a battery
cues.zh: 因为无论制造电池需要什么材料，其品位最高的“矿石”，

cues.en: is used batteries.
cues.zh: 其实就是废旧电池。

cues.en: We are already starting up processes where we grind up used lithium ion batteries and turn them into a mineral rich paste which, just like the raw ore we get out of the ground, can be processed into the raw material inputs that built that battery in the first place.
cues.zh: 我们已经开始建立这样的处理流程：把废旧锂离子电池粉碎成富含矿物质的浆料，就像从地里挖出来的原矿一样，这些浆料可以重新加工成最初制造电池所需的原材料。

cues.en: JerryRigEverything
cues.zh: JerryRigEverything

cues.en: has a two year old video about this process, and I'll link to it in the description if you'd like to see it.
cues.zh: 做过一期两年前的视频介绍过这个过程，如果你感兴趣，我会把链接放在简介里。

cues.en: Unlike fossil fuels where we toil away extracting and purifying resources
cues.zh: 相比化石燃料需要我们辛苦开采和提纯资源，

cues.en: just so that we can sell them, put them in our gas tanks, and set them on fire,
cues.zh: 只为了拿去卖掉、加进油箱然后一把火烧掉，

cues.en: when we're building a battery,
cues.zh: 当我们制造电池时，

cues.en: we're building something.
cues.zh: 我们是在创造实实在在的产物。

cues.en: We're extracting and purifying resources to make a durable good which will last many, many years.
cues.zh: 我们开采并提纯资源，是为了制造能用上很多很多年的耐用品。

cues.en: And because that durable good doesn't disappear once we've used it like fossil fuels do,
cues.zh: 而且与化石燃料不同，这种耐用品用完后并不会凭空消失，

cues.en: everything inside that durable good can be recovered.
cues.zh: 其中的一切成分都可以被回收。

cues.en: That's kind of the whole point of renewable energy. It's called renewable because it's not disposable.
cues.zh: 这正是可再生能源的核心意义。之所以叫“可再生”，是因为它不是一次性的。

cues.en: It's a resource we can use again and again and again without worrying about running out.
cues.zh: 这种资源我们可以循环反复使用，根本不用担心耗尽。

cues.en: Now a lot of people like to point out that we don't have a huge industry recycling lithium ion batteries yet.
cues.zh: 很多人喜欢指出，目前我们还没有形成庞大的锂电池回收产业。

cues.en: But that's mostly because we don't have a huge supply of dead lithium ion batteries yet.
cues.zh: 但这主要是因为目前还没有大量报废的锂电池。

cues.en: The biggest supply comes from electric cars with worn out battery packs. But again,
cues.zh: 最主要的报废来源是电池组损耗殆尽的电动车，但话说回来，

cues.en: modern battery chemistries and thermally controlled battery packs last decades.
cues.zh: 现代电池的化学体系和温控电池组寿命长达几十年。

cues.en: So aside from first gen Nissan Leafs, which had a uniquely terrible battery pack design,
cues.zh: 所以除了初代 Nissan Leaf 那种奇差无比的电池组设计之外，

cues.en: most electric cars that were built in the last fifteen years still have their original battery packs.
cues.zh: 过去十五年生产的大多数电动车依然在使用原装电池组。

cues.en: The biggest reason we end up with used packs is cars getting into collisions and becoming totaled.
cues.zh: 产生废旧电池组的最大原因，其实是车辆发生碰撞直接报废。

cues.en: That happens way more often than a battery pack failure.

cues.zh: 但其实事实并非如此。Trump 总统签署了几项行政命令，直接冻结了大部分资金，完全绕过了我们宪法的基本框架，

cues.en: which explicitly
cues.zh: 而宪法明确

cues.en: gives Congress the power of the purse.
cues.zh: 赋予了国会掌管财政大权的权力。

cues.en: We actually have a whole law, the Congressional Budget and Impoundment Control Act of 1974,
cues.zh: 我们甚至专门有一部法律，即 1974 年的《国会预算暨扣押控制法》（Congressional Budget and Impoundment Control Act of 1974），

cues.en: which explicitly makes what Trump did illegal.
cues.zh: 它明确规定了 Trump 的所作所为是违法的。

cues.en: But Republicans
cues.zh: 但共和党人

cues.en: currently control both houses of Congress, and they've made it very clear they do not care to provide the checks and balances they're constitutionally obligated to do.
cues.zh: 目前掌控着国会两院，而且他们态度很明确：根本不在乎履行宪法赋予他们的制衡职责。

cues.en: They're desecrating our constitution because they happen to be on the same team as the guy in the White House. And as we all know, the primary objective of this administration is to own the libs.
cues.zh: 他们正在践踏宪法，只因他们碰巧和白宫里那位是一伙的。众所周知，这届政府的首要目标就是恶心自由派。

cues.en: Or is it kidnapping brown people?
cues.zh: 还是说目标其实是绑架有色人种？

cues.en: It's getting kind of hard to tell.
cues.zh: 这事儿真是越来越说不清了。

cues.zh: 我从没想过，戴着面具、荷枪实弹的懦夫到处盘查“请出示证件”会出现在我三十岁人生的预测清单上，但它显然成真了。而且再仔细看看，我甚至连“白送的免费格”都没用就快凑齐一整行了。

cues.en: I've already crossed off, threatened to invade Greenland and destroy NATO, threatened to annex Canada, and papers please, so all I need now is a few murders of US citizens which were captured on video from multiple angles.
cues.zh: 我已经划掉了“威胁入侵格陵兰并摧毁北约”、“威胁吞并加拿大”以及“请出示证件”，现在就差几起被多角度视频拍下的美国公民遇害事件了。

cues.en: What's that?
cues.zh: 那是什么？

cues.en: Cross that off too?
cues.zh: 那个也要划掉？

cues.en: Well, surely I'm not gonna be able to cross off government officials telling us our eyes didn't see what saw.
cues.zh: 呃，我总不可能划掉“政府官员坚称我们亲眼所见的不是事实”吧。

cues.en: Oh.
cues.zh: 哦。

cues.en: Bingo.
cues.zh: 中了。

cues.en: Folks, you need to wake up and smell the fascism.
cues.zh: 各位，该醒醒了，闻闻这法西斯的气味吧。

cues.en: I don't know what imaginary lines you might have drawn which could be crossed,
cues.zh: 我不知道你们心里划过什么不可逾越的红线，

cues.en: But if you can't agree we've crossed a very bad one, you need to get off Twitter and stop watching Fox News or Newsmax or OANN or whatever those new ones are or,
cues.zh: 但如果你们还不承认我们已经踩了一条极其恶劣的红线，那就赶紧关掉 Twitter，别再看 Fox News、Newsmax、OANN 或者那些乱七八糟的新媒体了，甚至是……

cues.en: I'm so sad to say,
cues.zh: 我很难过地说，

cues.en: CBS News.
cues.zh: 还有 CBS News。

cues.en: It's bad.
cues.zh: 真的很糟糕。

cues.en: We're clearly living under leaders who have a completely different understanding of reality than the rest of us do. And they are so high on their own supply that their followers will believe abject lies.
cues.zh: 很显然，领导我们的这些人对现实的认知和我们完全脱节。他们彻底沉醉于自己的谎言，以至于追随者对彻头彻尾的谎言也深信不疑。

cues.en: Renewable energy is only controversial because they made it so.
cues.zh: 可再生能源之所以有争议，纯粹是他们一手炒作出来的。

cues.en: And they don't want you thinking through the reality which is free energy from reusable materials as I've just explained.
cues.zh: 他们不想让你们看清现实，也就是我刚才解释的：利用可循环材料获取免费能源。

cues.en: They have donors who still make money selling you fossil fuels, and so they do not want you thinking about how much you're spending and how we have the opportunity to stop.
cues.zh: 他们的金主还在靠向你们兜售化石燃料赚钱，所以他们不想让你们算算自己花了多少钱，也不想让你们知道我们其实有机会摆脱这一切。

cues.en: Even worse,
cues.zh: 更糟糕的是，

cues.en: they'll artificially lower the cost of fossil fuels through subsidies
cues.zh: 他们还会通过补贴人为压低化石燃料的成本，

cues.en: even though they're supposedly the party against that sort of thing.
cues.zh: 尽管他们明面上自称是反对这种干预的党派。

cues.en: I am very scared of what the future of this country looks like.
cues.zh: 我非常害怕这个国家未来的样子。

cues.en: The Bill of Rights looks to be effectively dead.
cues.zh: 《权利法案》看起来已经名存实亡了。

cues.en: Our First Amendment right to protest is being challenged through intimidation,
cues.zh: 我们宪法第一修正案保障的抗议权利正受到恐吓威胁，

cues.en: and the press that dares to tell the truth is being declared an enemy of the people.
cues.zh: 敢于讲真话的新闻界被扣上了“人民公敌”的帽子。

cues.en: Our Fourth Amendment right to be free of unreasonable searches and seizures is being gleefully violated and nobody seems to care.
cues.zh: 我们宪法第四修正案保障的免受无理搜查与扣押的权利被肆意践踏，却似乎没人真正在乎。

cues.en: Even the Second Amendment
cues.zh: 就连第二修正案

cues.en: might as well be lost. Our government used the fact that Alex Preti, a legal firearm holder with a concealed carry permit, had a gun on him to justify his murder.
cues.zh: 恐怕也名存实亡了。Alex Preti 是持有隐蔽持枪证的合法持枪人，但我们的政府却拿他当时随身带枪作为借口，来为谋杀他开脱。

cues.en: So do we have a right to bear arms or not?
cues.zh: 所以我们到底有没有持枪权？

cues.en: Sure doesn't seem like it.
cues.zh: 看着可真不像有。

cues.en: If you're upset that a tech creator like myself is suddenly being explicit about politics,
cues.zh: 如果你因为我这样一个科技创作者突然大谈政治而感到不满，

cues.en: then you're not paying enough attention and are part of the problem.
cues.zh: 那说明你根本没有看清局势，而且你自己也是问题的一部分。

cues.en: I should not have to do this. I never thought I'd be making a video where I said, hey guys, remember that whole constitution
cues.zh: 我本不必做这些。我也从未想过自己会拍视频说：嘿伙计们，还记得宪法那档子

cues.en: thing?
cues.zh: 事吗？

cues.en: I figured our leaders would always uphold it but they're clearly not.
cues.zh: 我本以为我们的领导人总会捍卫宪法，但显然并没有。

cues.en: The document does not enforce itself and so it is up to us.
cues.zh: 法律文本不会自我执行，这得靠我们自己。

cues.en: We had a revolution in 1776
cues.zh: 我们在 1776 年掀起了一场革命，

cues.en: to escape the tyranny of British rule and the Declaration of Independence describes what's going on right now with distressing clarity.
cues.zh: 就是为了摆脱英国统治的暴政，而《独立宣言》对当下现状的描述，清醒得令人心惊。

cues.en: Let me quote it for you. He has kept among us, in times of peace, standing armies without the consent of our legislatures.
cues.zh: 让我给你们念一段：“未经我们立法机关的同意，在和平时期，他在我们当中驻扎常备军。”

cues.en: He has affected to render the military independent of and superior to the civil power.
cues.zh: 他极力使军队独立于民权，并凌驾于民权之上。

cues.en: He has combined with others to subject us to a jurisdiction foreign to our constitution and unacknowledged by our laws,
cues.zh: 他与其他人勾结，把我们置于不受宪法认可、未经法律允许的管辖之下，

cues.en: giving his assent to their acts of pretended legislation.
cues.zh: 批准他们炮制的各种伪立法。

cues.en: For quartering large bodies of armed troops among us, for protecting them by a mock trial from punishment for any murders which they should commit on the inhabitants of these states,
cues.zh: 在我们中间驻扎大批武装部队；用假审判包庇他们杀害这些州居民的罪行；

cues.en: for cutting off our trade with all parts of the world,
cues.zh: 切断我们与世界各地的贸易；

cues.en: for imposing taxes on us without our consent,
cues.zh: 未经我们同意就向我们强行征税；

cues.en: for depriving us in many cases of the benefit of trial by jury,
cues.zh: 在许多案件中剥夺我们享有陪审团审判的权利；

cues.en: for transporting us beyond seas to be tried for pretended offenses.
cues.zh: 把我们押送海外，以莫须有的罪名进行审判。

cues.en: Those words were written about King George,
cues.zh: 这些话当年写的是 King George，

cues.en: but they might as well describe Donald Trump.
cues.zh: 但拿来形容 Donald Trump 也完全说得通。

cues.en: We
cues.zh: 我们

cues.en: fought the Revolutionary War to be free of tyrannical kings, but it looks like we're under tyranny again inflicted on ourselves.
cues.zh: 当年打独立战争是为了摆脱暴君统治，可现在看来，我们又陷入了自找的专制之中。

cues.en: You may have been one of those people who likes to stay out of politics but politics eventually comes for everyone.
cues.zh: 你以前可能习惯远离政治，但政治终究会找上每个人。

cues.en: Here we are.
cues.zh: 现实就是如此。

cues.en: For the love of God,
cues.zh: 拜托大家，

cues.en: please learn from this and remember what happens when you stop paying attention and let other people think for you.
cues.zh: 请吸取教训，记住当你不再关心、任由别人替你思考时会发生什么。

cues.en: It doesn't end well.
cues.zh: 那绝不会有什么好下场。

cues.en: Now, as scared as I am, I am still going to vote in the midterms and I will be voting against Republicans.
cues.zh: 现在，尽管我也很害怕，但我依然会在中期选举中投票，并且坚决不投共和党。

cues.en: I think you should too.
cues.zh: 我觉得你也应该这么做。

cues.en: And yes, because the realities of our terrible two party system don't always sink into everyone.
cues.zh: 确实，因为并非所有人都能真正看清我们这糟糕的两党制现实。

cues.en: I am saying I think you should vote for Democrats in November.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得大家在 11 月应该把票投给民主党。

cues.en: I am not a huge fan of a lot of what the Democratic party is up to these days.
cues.zh: 我对民主党近来的很多所作所为也并不太感冒。

cues.en: They seem unfortunately to be far more beholden to corporate interests than they're concerned with the lives of their constituents.
cues.zh: 遗憾的是，比起关心选民的生活，他们似乎远更受制于企业利益。

cues.en: Universal healthcare still hasn't happened and the best reason I can think that's the case is that the for profit healthcare lobby is very influential.
cues.zh: 全民医保至今未能实现，我能想到的最大原因就是营利性医疗游说集团的势力太大了。

cues.en: Meanwhile,
cues.zh: 与此同时，

cues.en: constituents such as myself haven't even been able to leave a voicemail at any of senator Durbin's offices because they're all all the inboxes are full.
cues.zh: 像我这样的选民甚至没法在参议员 Durbin 的任何办公室留言，因为所有的语音信箱全满了。

cues.en: They've been very disappointing.
cues.zh: 他们确实让人非常失望。

cues.en: But right now, we're heading into a primary season and you'll have the opportunity to vote in those primaries very soon to tell Democrats how you want them to act.
cues.zh: 但眼下我们正进入初选季，很快你就有机会通过投票，明确告诉民主党你希望他们怎么做。

cues.en: Please make sure you're registered to vote in general and in the Democratic primary if that's required in your state.
cues.zh: 请务必确保自己完成了选民登记，如果你们州有要求，也要登记参加民主党初选。

cues.en: If you don't know how to do that, call or walk into your local library.
cues.zh: 如果你不知道该怎么做，可以打电话或直接去一趟当地的图书馆。

cues.en: The people there have the same mission I do, to share knowledge and be helpful,
cues.zh: 那里的人和我的使命一样，都是为了分享知识、提供帮助，

cues.en: and they'll guide you.
cues.zh: 他们会给你指导。

cues.en: Be sure you ask them how the primary process works in your state and whether you need to declare a party affiliation to vote in it. And by the way, just throwing this out there, the process of registering to vote is how we verify the citizenship of voters.
cues.zh: 一定要问清楚你们州的初选流程，以及投票是否需要声明党派属性。顺便提一句，选民登记这个过程，本就是核验投票人公民身份的方式。

cues.en: You have to be on the voter rolls before you can cast a vote.
cues.zh: 你必须先登记在选民册上，才能投票。

cues.en: But it's a lot easier for Republicans to ignore that fact and lie by omission to make you think massive voter fraud from non citizens keeps happening.
cues.zh: 但对共和党人来说，无视这个事实、靠隐瞒来撒谎，让你以为非公民大规模选民欺诈一直在发生，要容易得多。

cues.en: They lie all the time and people need to stop listening to them.
cues.zh: 他们总在撒谎，大家别再听他们的了。

cues.en: This isn't just normal politicians always lie stuff. This is active propaganda
cues.zh: 这不只是政客总爱撒谎的寻常把戏。这是有目的的宣传。

cues.en: designed to make you distrustful of your fellow human beings. It's disgusting and shameful.
cues.zh: 旨在让你不信任自己的同胞。这既恶心又可耻。

cues.en: How did we get to a place where the president can say other countries pay for tariffs and literally nobody cares that he's lying?
cues.zh: 我们怎么会走到这一步——总统可以说关税由其他国家买单，却几乎没人在意他在撒谎？

cues.en: He's counting on his base not understanding
cues.zh: 他指望他的基本盘不懂这一点。

cues.en: that you can't just charge someone extra money when you buy something from them because
cues.zh: 你从别人那里买东西时，不能反过来向对方多收钱，因为

cues.en: that's just not how trade works.
cues.zh: 贸易根本不是这么运作的。

cues.en: Hell, that's not even how commerce works.
cues.zh: 见鬼，商业运作都不是这样。

cues.en: I can't walk into Menards and demand they pay me to buy their products.
cues.zh: 我总不能走进 Menards，要求他们付钱让我买他们的产品。

cues.en: But the only people who are willing to say that plainly
cues.zh: 但唯一愿意直说这一点的人

cues.en: were independent journalists and freaking YouTubers.
cues.zh: 竟然是独立记者和见鬼的 YouTuber。

cues.en: The stalwarts of the press just kept writing headlines as if reality was up for debate, and they still haven't cut that shit out.
cues.zh: 新闻界的中坚们照旧写标题，仿佛现实还有得争，而且他们至今没改掉这烂毛病。

cues.en: It is terrifying
cues.zh: 这令人恐惧。

cues.en: how nobody is interested in holding anyone accountable for anything these days.
cues.zh: 如今竟没人愿意为任何事追究任何人的责任。

cues.en: But while I am terrified,
cues.zh: 但在我感到恐惧的同时，

cues.en: I am also increasingly hopeful.
cues.zh: 我也越来越有希望。

cues.en: The people of Minnesota are demonstrating what we have to do.
cues.zh: 明尼苏达州的人民正在示范我们该怎么做。

cues.en: We have to care for each other.
cues.zh: 我们必须互相关心。

cues.en: Don't wait for someone to lend a helping hand. Be that helping hand.
cues.zh: 别等别人伸出援手。你自己就去当那只援手。

cues.en: Organizing networks are popping up everywhere because those of us who manage to grow up
cues.zh: 组织网络正在各地涌现，因为我们当中那些好不容易长大

cues.en: into adults
cues.zh: 成为成年人

cues.en: who care about people other than ourselves
cues.zh: 并且关心他人而不只是自己的人

cues.en: are not going to stand by and let this illegitimate government run by petulant toddlers
cues.zh: 不会袖手旁观，让这个由任性幼儿把持的非法政府

cues.en: violate the constitution and the very principles that make America great.
cues.zh: 去践踏宪法和让美国伟大的那些根本原则。

cues.en: My fellow Midwesterners in Minnesota have made me so proud.
cues.zh: 明尼苏达的各位中西部同胞让我无比自豪。

cues.en: Stay strong
cues.zh: 保持坚强

cues.en: and keep teaching us how to be brave and resist this horrible chapter of our history with steadfast,
cues.zh: 并继续教我们如何勇敢，如何去抵抗我们历史上这可怕的一章，

cues.en: nonviolent defiance.
cues.zh: 以坚定的、非暴力反抗。

cues.en: Immigration and Customs Enforcement is a lawless group of masked thugs terrorizing our cities and neighbors for daring to look not quite white.
cues.zh: 移民和海关执法局是一群无法无天的蒙面暴徒，恐吓我们的城市和邻居，只因为他们胆敢看起来不那么白。

cues.en: Anyone who has any understanding of history will know that it is happening here.
cues.zh: 任何了解历史的人都会知道，这种事正在这里发生。

cues.en: And if you believe that to be true, then you should also believe that ice must be abolished.
cues.zh: 如果你相信这是真的，那你也应该相信 ICE 必须被废除。

cues.en: And if that freaks you out, I'm gonna guess you've been told the people who say that want completely open borders.
cues.zh: 如果这让你抓狂，我猜你被告知过，说这话的人想要完全开放边境。

cues.en: Some people do, but most people simply took the poem on the Statue Of Liberty as meaningful
cues.zh: 有些人确实如此，但大多数人只是把自由女神像上的那首诗当回事，

cues.en: and think this country should open its arms wide and provide a legal pathway to immigration just as our ancestors did on the storied Ellis Island.
cues.zh: 并认为这个国家应该张开双臂，提供合法的移民途径，就像我们的祖先在著名的埃利斯岛所做的那样。

cues.en: It is our decades long inability to have true immigration reform occur which put us in this place and what we're doing today to fix it is clearly
cues.zh: 正是我们几十年来无法实现真正的移民改革，才让我们落到这个地步；而我们今天为解决它所做的，显然

cues.en: wrong.
cues.zh: 是错的。

cues.en: It is a racist, ethnic cleansing operation happening on the pretext of child care fraud which was already being investigated and dealt with by the state of Minnesota but which some terminally online weirdos
cues.zh: 这是一场以儿童保育欺诈为借口的、种族主义的种族清洗行动；那件事明尼苏达州早就在调查处理，但一些沉迷网络的怪人

cues.en: somehow got wind of and spun into this madness.
cues.zh: 不知怎么得知了，还把它炒作成这场疯狂。

cues.en: And that madness is being perpetrated by agents of the state and endorsed
cues.zh: 而这场疯狂正由政府人员实施，并得到

cues.en: by Republicans.
cues.zh: 共和党人的支持。

cues.en: Republicans could stop this now,
cues.zh: 共和党人现在就可以阻止这一切，

cues.en: but they won't.
cues.zh: 但他们不会。

cues.en: And the reason I know we absolutely can abolish ICE?
cues.zh: 而我为什么知道我们绝对能废除 ICE？

cues.en: I am older than ICE. In fact, I'm older than the entire Department of Homeland Security.
cues.zh: 我比 ICE 还老。事实上，我比整个国土安全部还老。

cues.en: That agency was created post 09/11. And in retrospect,
cues.zh: 那个机构是 9/11 之后成立的。回过头看，

cues.en: the folks who thought, Homeland Security sounds kinda ominous,
cues.zh: 那些觉得“国土安全”听起来有点不祥的人，

cues.en: were apparently correct.
cues.zh: 显然是对的。

cues.en: We need to throw this system out and start over. And so, yes, I believe ICE must be abolished. There is no reforming that agency of thugs. It has to go.
cues.zh: 我们需要抛弃这个体系，重新开始。所以，是的，我认为必须废除 ICE。那个由暴徒组成的机构没法改革。它必须消失。

cues.en: And the lawless criminals hiding behind masks who are violating the Fourth Amendment day in and day out need to be prosecuted
cues.zh: 而那些躲在面具后面、天天违反第四修正案的不法罪犯，必须被起诉

cues.en: for each and every one of their crimes.
cues.zh: 为他们犯下的每一项罪行。

cues.en: I will be voting in the primaries, and I sure as well hope my representative Sean Kasten starts saying that with clarity and conviction.
cues.zh: 我会在初选中投票，我也当然希望我的代表 Sean Kasten 开始明确而坚定地这么说。

cues.en: Sean has been one of the people who understand the realities of renewable energy and has been a long time advocate of it so we've been pretty aligned. But we're not aligned on everything and my patience is starting to break.
cues.zh: Sean 一直是理解可再生能源现实的人之一，也是长期倡导者，所以我们一直相当一致。但我们并非在所有事情上都一致，我的耐心快绷不住了。

cues.en: So if you made it here,
cues.zh: 所以如果你看到了这里，

cues.en: thank you for watching.
cues.zh: 感谢观看。

cues.en: I hope we can bring some sanity back to this country and that we can start calling lies what they are.
cues.zh: 我希望我们能给这个国家带回一些理智，并开始把谎言称作谎言。

cues.en: And you will have to be a part of that.
cues.zh: 而你必须参与其中。

cues.en: Talk to your neighbors, talk to your family,
cues.zh: 和你的邻居谈谈，和你的家人谈谈，

cues.en: and if you don't know where to start the conversation,
cues.zh: 如果你不知道从哪里开始对话，

cues.en: that's why there's that fake ending.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么会有那个假结尾。

cues.en: If you think it might get some gears turning, go ahead and watch this video with someone and stop it there. See how it goes. And if you want to send it to someone with a link, there's an unlisted version of this video on my second channel which actually stops at the fake ending.
cues.zh: 如果你觉得这能让思路转起来，那就和某人一起看这个视频，并在那里停下。看看会怎么样。如果你想用链接发给别人，我的第二频道上有一个不公开版本，它实际上就停在假结尾处。

cues.en: The link is in the description and a card should be popping up now.
cues.zh: 链接在简介里，现在应该会弹出一张卡片。

cues.en: I would pin a comment too, but I am not interested in knowing just what sort of replies that will get.
cues.zh: 我也想置顶一条评论，但我没兴趣知道那会招来什么样的回复。

cues.en: I am all but certain it will be depressing.
cues.zh: 我几乎可以肯定，那会令人沮丧。

cues.en: The future has always been in our collective hands,
cues.zh: 未来一直掌握在我们集体手中，

cues.en: But we need to stop tolerating lies.
cues.zh: 但我们必须停止容忍谎言。

cues.en: We need to stop tolerating greed.
cues.zh: 我们必须停止容忍贪婪。

cues.en: And we need to stop tolerating politicians
cues.zh: 而且我们必须停止容忍这样的政客

cues.en: who care more about their corporate donors than they do their constituents.
cues.zh: 他们关心企业捐赠者胜过关心自己的选民。

cues.en: We need to care about our future more than we care about the price of eggs or the price of gas.
cues.zh: 比起鸡蛋或汽油的价格，我们更应该关心自己的未来。

cues.en: And most importantly,
cues.zh: 最重要的是，

cues.en: we need to care for each other.
cues.zh: 我们要关爱彼此。

cues.en: There is a duty of care in everything we do and that's the simplest way to put my personal politics.
cues.zh: 我们所做的一切都负有关怀的责任，这也是我个人政治理念最简明的概括。

cues.en: Start acting like you take that duty seriously.
cues.zh: 真正把这份责任当回事，行动起来吧。

cues.en: A free future depends on it. A future with liberty
cues.zh: 自由的未来全系于此。一个享有自由

cues.en: and justice
cues.zh: 与正义，

cues.en: for all.
cues.zh: 属于所有人的未来。
